correctness.rationale: Polar equations give theta-dot=1 and d(r^-3)/dt=-3A(theta), so conserved K=r^-3+P(theta). Periodicity iff K>maxP; K<=maxP reaches zero radial inverse cube at finite forward angle (escape in original time). The area integral is one half of angular min{R^2,(M-P)^(-2/3)}. A(theta) is a first/third-harmonic trigonometric cubic satisfying A^(4)+10Asecond+9A=0; nonzero A cannot have fourth-order zero, so maxima of P are exactly order 2 or 4. Rescaling near each maximum by R^(-3/k) gives integrable limiting tail |v|^(-2k/3) and constant (2k)/(2k-3)c^(-1/k). For critical K=M, r~c^(-1/3)(t*-t)^(-k/3). Independently checked angular examples -y(x²+y²), -y³ with contact coefficients 3/2,3/4; inspected finite quadrature verifier only supports examples.
